{{short description|Italian mathematician}}
'''Ferdinando 'Teo' Mora'''{{efn|Teo Mora is his nickname, but used in most of his post-1980s publications; he has also used the [[pen name]] Theo Moriarty.}} is an Italian [[mathematician]], and since 1990 until 2019 a professor of [[Algebraic geometry#Computational algebraic geometry|algebra]] at the [[University of Genoa]].

== Life and work ==
Mora's degree is in mathematics from the [[University of Genoa]] in 1974. Mora's [[#Further_reading|publications]] span forty years; his notable contributions in [[computer algebra]] are the 
[[tangent cone]] algorithm<ref>[[#mora82|An algorithm to compute the equations of tangent cones]]; [[#PMT|An introduction to the tangent cone algorithm]].</ref><ref>Better algorithms due to [[#GP|Greuel-Pfister]] and [[#GR|Gräbe]] are currently available.</ref> and its extension of [[Bruno Buchberger|Buchberger]] theory of [[Gröbner bases]] and related [[Buchberger's algorithm|algorithm]] earlier<ref>[[#mora85|Gröbner bases for non-commutative polynomial rings]].</ref> to non-commutative [[polynomial ring]]s<ref>Extending the proposal set by [[#Diamond|George M. Bergman]].</ref> and more recently<ref>[[#NG4|De Nugis Groebnerialium 4: Zacharias, Spears, Möller]], [[#Ceria|Buchberger–Weispfenning theory for effective associative rings]]; see also [[#7Var|Seven variations on standard bases]].</ref> to effective rings; less significant<ref>The result is a weaker version of the result presented  
[[#BayerMorrison|in the same issue of the journal]] 
by Bayer and Morrison.</ref> the notion of [[Gröbner fan]]; marginal, with respect to the other authors, his contribution to the [[FGLM algorithm]].

* [[#mora84|1984 paper]] on [[Gröbner bases]] and bounding the degree thereof

* [[#mora16|2016 book-volume]], ''Solving Polynomial Equation Systems IV: [[Bruno Buchberger|Buchberger]] Theory and Beyond'', on the [[Buchberger algorithm]]

Mora is on the [[scientific peer review|managing-editorial-board]] of the journal ''Applicable Algebra in Engineering, Communication and Computing'' published by [[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]],<ref name=aaeccBoard/> and was also formerly an editor of the ''Bulletin of the [[Iranian Mathematical Society]]''.
<!--{{efn|See [http://www.disi.unige.it/person/MoraF/ previous faculty-page].}}-->

He is the author of the tetralogy ''Solving Polynomial Equation Systems'':
* ''Solving Polynomial Equation Systems I: The [[Kronecker]]-[[Duval]] Philosophy'', on equations [[Univariate polynomial#Equations|in one variable]]<ref name=roberts06/>
* ''Solving Polynomial Equation Systems II: [[Francis Sowerby Macaulay|Macaulay]]'s paradigm and [[Gröbner bases|Gröbner]] technology'', on [[system of polynomial equations|equations in several variables]]<ref name=coutinho09/><ref name=roberts06/>
* ''Solving Polynomial Equation Systems III: Algebraic Solving'', 
* ''Solving Polynomial Equation Systems IV: [[Bruno Buchberger|Buchberger]] Theory and Beyond'', on the [[Buchberger algorithm]]

== Personal life ==
<!--''{{illm|Storia del cinema dell'orrore|it|Storia del cinema dell'orrore (saggio)}}''-->
Mora lives in [[Genoa]].<ref name=repubblica2002/>  Mora published a [[#mora77|book trilogy in 1977-1978]] (reprinted 2001-2003) called ''Storia del cinema dell'orrore'' on the [[Horror film#History|history of horror films]].<ref name=repubblica2002/>  [[Radiotelevisione Italiana|Italian television]] said in 2014 that the books are an "authoritative guide with in-depth detailed descriptions and analysis."<ref name=rai2014/>
